opportunity_name: Trans-Caspian fibre-optic route: landing stations and network nodes
investor_capital_decision: Telecom infrastructure investor funds the named Aktau-Sumgait cable and landing/network infrastructure as one route decision.
buyer_market: Carriers and data-service operators buying Europe-Asia connectivity.
why_now: FACT: construction completed; official launch on 15 Oct 2026, superseding the card's construction-stage trigger.
strongest_realistic_alternative: The same route already funded by Kazakhtelecom/AzerTelecom; existing terrestrial transit is the customer alternative.
deciding_location_factor: Access to ownership and completion capital in the specified route, before latency or transit pricing.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: Kazakhstan is already an endpoint of the incumbent project; it cannot win this already-committed build decision again.
scale_view: Strategic route exists; merchant demand is irrelevant once the specific build slot is captured.
physical_constraint_view: Construction and official launch evidenced; no claim that all downstream capacity is commercially utilised.
captured_status: FACT: sponsors completed and launched the identified route. No distinct additional asset or stake sale is specified in the admitted hypothesis.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: capacity/connection revenue accrues to route owners; no new investor entitlement demonstrated.
cheapest_kill_test: Is this route still an unallocated construction/ownership investment?
decisive_evidence: FACT: NEQSOL release says construction complete (2 Oct); Akorda says launched by the two operators (15 Oct), S01-S02.
key_unknown: Whether a separately documented sale or expansion might later exist; not assumed or substituted here.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: FAIL as framed because the identified route-build decision has already been executed by incumbents, not because telecom demand is absent. A new stake sale or separate node would require explicit evidence and review of scope.

investor_capital_decision: Veterinary-vaccine manufacturer considers production investment; product, site and partner opening remain unspecified.
buyer_market: State veterinary procurement and livestock customers; regional access unproven.
why_now: FACT: national FMD-free status is with vaccination; maintaining status does not eliminate vaccine purchasing.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Existing licensed OtarBioPharm/QazBioPharm partnership and established imports; strongest product-specific supplier unresolved.
deciding_location_factor: Unserved purchasing contracts and available commercial production/partnership slot.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: local continuity of supply could matter; an existing partnership already pursues this benefit.
scale_view: Recurring purchasing is plausible; addressable volumes and an incremental contract not established.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: available approved commercial capacity/site; restricted validation not undertaken.
captured_status: Historical company plan identifies a Boehringer agreement, not proof of achieved 2026 output or full market capture.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: contracted product sales and reliable local supply; price/capacity economics unverified.
cheapest_kill_test: Do existing licensed supply arrangements already cover the commercial demand?
decisive_evidence: FACT: WOAH status with vaccination (S03); historical company partnership/production plan (S04). Plans are not operating output.
key_unknown: Manual business review of remaining demand, procurement access and an open capital slot; further validation incomplete.
next_test_if_uwt: Human commercial reviewer: check current procurement awards, business-level output disclosures and partner availability; 45-minute desk review. No biological methods or experiments.
pass_condition_if_uwt: Permitted commercial evidence establishes material unserved demand, an available investment slot and credible pricing versus existing supply.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: PARK if commercially reachable demand is already covered or too small; FAIL only on a separately evidenced fatal commercial contradiction. Access limitation alone never kills it.
screening_rationale: UWT — manual review required due to research-access limitation. Preserve business-level demand and partner evidence only; limitation is not evidence against the investment.

opportunity_name: Flat-glass production near planned soda ash capacity
investor_capital_decision: Flat-glass maker builds or expands capacity linked to Zhambyl soda ash; greenfield/expansion entry remains unresolved.
buyer_market: Kazakh construction-glass buyers; export demand must be measured net of freight and rivals.
why_now: FACT: contractor reports soda-ash construction in Mar 2026; October environmental hearing exists. Commissioning is not verified.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Orda Glass brownfield output/expansion in Kyzylorda before Turkey/Uzbekistan import supply.
deciding_location_factor: Delivered glass cost at viable furnace utilisation, including gas and soda-ash price.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: domestic soda can reduce input freight but also benefits the operating domestic competitor; no exclusive location rent.
scale_view: FACT: Orda has about 197 kt/year capacity. Residual demand for another furnace is UNKNOWN.
physical_constraint_view: Gas, continuous power, water and sand quality at the proposed glass site not secured; soda hearing is not delivered feedstock.
captured_status: Existing float plant operating; soda under development. Neither proves every incremental glass slot captured.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: saved finished-glass freight and potentially cheaper soda; utilisation is the swing variable.
cheapest_kill_test: Is soda construction real, and can residual glass demand load additional capacity?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S05-S06 support live soda development; S07 confirms an operating flat-glass incumbent, not a vacant domestic market.
key_unknown: Residual saleable tonnes and delivered cost versus Orda expansion, including dependable soda supply.
next_test_if_uwt: Batch 04 commercial reviewer, 60 minutes: reconcile recent glass imports/output by product, obtain Orda expansion status and compare gas/soda/freight quotes for an additional furnace.
pass_condition_if_uwt: Residual buyer volumes meet vendor minimum viable utilisation and delivered cost beats Orda expansion/imports with supply and utility commitments.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: FAIL if verified utilities or supply make the stated plant infeasible; PARK if spare incumbent capacity or cheaper imports leave inadequate utilisation.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT; the cheapest soda-status kill does not fire, but the same input advantage is available to a strong incumbent.

opportunity_name: Ion-exchange resin manufacture for uranium ISR
investor_capital_decision: Specialty-resin producer builds manufacturing capacity serving southern Kazakhstan ISR operators; no site/technology investor named.
buyer_market: Kazatomprom and uranium JVs purchasing replacement resin; fresh resin volumes are not uranium output.
why_now: FACT: issuer has a resin procurement strategy and ongoing wellfield development; a resin shortage is not established.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Qualified imported resin under central procurement and stockholding; strongest supplier not established.
deciding_location_factor: Qualified resin lifetime cost at commercially viable manufacturing scale.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: proximity can reduce inventory/lead time; imported chemical inputs and global factory scale may outweigh it.
scale_view: A concentrated real buyer exists; annual fresh-resin replacement tonnage and minimum line scale UNKNOWN.
physical_constraint_view: Chemical feed supply, environmental permission, utilities and manufacturing know-how not established at a specific site.
captured_status: Procurement exists; no evidence of a captured local manufacturing slot or an open plant tender.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: sale margin plus supply-security value only if performance-adjusted cost competes with imports.
cheapest_kill_test: Does annual qualified fresh-resin demand load a viable local manufacturing line?
decisive_evidence: FACT: 2024 issuer report p.136 names resin procurement strategy (S08); 2026 development plans (S09). No sourced resin TAM.
key_unknown: Minimum economic plant scale versus contracted replacement demand and incumbent delivered price.
next_test_if_uwt: Batch 04 commercial reviewer, 60 minutes: extract three years of fresh-resin purchase quantities/prices; obtain a manufacturer's minimum line and qualified delivered-cost indication.
pass_condition_if_uwt: Contractable quantities support minimum plant scale and lifetime cost is at or below qualified imported supply without assuming a shortage premium.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: PARK if local demand sits below economic scale or stocking imported resin solves the problem more cheaply; FAIL only on proven unavailable essential rights/input.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT; recurring consumable demand provides a testable anchor, but uranium scale alone cannot justify resin manufacture.

opportunity_name: Lu-177 production with the Institute of Nuclear Physics
investor_capital_decision: Radiopharmaceutical/isotope supplier invests with INP in Almaty Lu-177 commercial capacity; partnership availability unconfirmed.
buyer_market: Therapy-product manufacturers and hospitals; accessible product-specific export demand UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT: January 2026 government update names Lu-177 localisation among live INP investment projects.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Established international Lu-177 suppliers and INP's own already-funded project; exact strongest supplier unresolved.
deciding_location_factor: Buyer-approved product availability and reliable delivered supply, not reactor ownership alone.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: existing INP infrastructure may save entry cost; existing broad GMP accreditation does not establish approval of the proposed product.
scale_view: The cited 85% domestic share covers broader radiopharmaceuticals, not Lu-177; no product TAM established.
physical_constraint_view: Commercial product approvals, dependable transport and available licensed site capacity remain unresolved; no process work performed.
captured_status: Localisation project exists; no disclosed partner/stake opening verified, and no evidence all incremental commercial capacity is allocated.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: product supply margin using existing infrastructure, conditional on approved buyers and reliable delivery.
cheapest_kill_test: Does an investable Lu-177 slot remain after existing INP commitments?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S11 names Lu-177 investment project separately from existing product supply and broader market share.
key_unknown: Open partner slot, approved saleable product and buyer commitments at a competitive delivered price.
next_test_if_uwt: Batch 04 commercial reviewer, 60 minutes: review INP's public project/partner notices and product approvals; compare business-level supply terms from two established suppliers and one buyer.
pass_condition_if_uwt: An available capital slot and buyer-accepted supply can use existing infrastructure at a competitive delivered margin and viable contracted volume.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: PARK if the project is already fully allocated or local sales cannot support scale; FAIL only if a necessary market-access right is demonstrably unavailable.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT; specific asset and commercial project exist, but approval of other products cannot be inherited.

opportunity_name: Wellfield drilling services for uranium ISR
investor_capital_decision: Drilling contractor funds rigs and service capacity at southern ISR wellfields.
buyer_market: Kazatomprom/JV wellfield-development purchasers; contracted drill-metres, not uranium sales, are the market.
why_now: FACT: issuer expects additional drilling and well construction in 2026 development spending.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Volkovgeology/internal capacity and existing local contractors; imported rigs operated locally, not remote pipe suppliers.
deciding_location_factor: Qualified delivered cost per completed well and rig utilisation under accessible contracts.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: on-site presence is necessary but shared by incumbents; new rigs need a capacity/productivity gap.
scale_view: Recurring wellfield spend is real; announced total mining capex is not drilling TAM.
physical_constraint_view: Mobilisation, service permissions, qualified staff and site consumables must be secured; existing rig programme confirms local capability.
captured_status: Incumbent developing domestic rigs; no evidence all future metres allocated, nor an established foreign-contractor opening.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: contracted service margin and high utilisation reduce idle-rig capital burden.
cheapest_kill_test: Are any profitable drill-metres available after incumbent and internal rig capacity?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S09 supports active wellfield development; S10 supports an active incumbent rig/productivity programme.
key_unknown: Contestable contract volumes, rig-day productivity and incumbent spare capacity.
next_test_if_uwt: Batch 04 commercial reviewer, 60 minutes: compare 2025-26 wellfield tender awards/metres with incumbent rig-days; check one forthcoming bid's eligibility and indicative unit price.
pass_condition_if_uwt: Eligible contestable metres keep an incremental rig fleet above break-even utilisation at a cost competitive with internal/local drilling.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: PARK if incumbents can cover demand below entrant break-even cost; FAIL if a verified procurement restriction excludes the investor business model.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT; the capital need is tangible, while proximity alone is not a competitive advantage.

investor_capital_decision: Catalyst-service investor builds a domestic regeneration facility; site and commercial process scope are unspecified.
buyer_market: Atyrau, Pavlodar and Shymkent refinery buyers plus petrochemicals; only regenerable purchased lots count.
why_now: FACT: refineries operate and are upgrading; no regeneration-specific shortage or new open contract verified.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Existing in-unit regeneration and established off-site regenerators; replacement catalyst where reuse is uneconomic.
deciding_location_factor: Accepted regenerated-catalyst cost/performance and annual throughput versus external service.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: fewer cross-border shipments and quicker turnaround can save money; dispersed small lots can destroy scale.
scale_view: Refinery crude throughput cannot be treated as regeneration TAM; regenerable tonnes/cycle UNKNOWN.
physical_constraint_view: Environmental/waste permissions, site utilities and handling routes unverified; no national utility capacity assumed.
captured_status: Global service model demonstrated; Kazakhstan service awards and spare capacity not established.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: regeneration fee and avoided replacement/logistics cost; no precious-metal-recovery business substituted.
cheapest_kill_test: How many catalyst tonnes actually require external regeneration rather than in-unit treatment or disposal?
decisive_evidence: FACT: named refinery operations/upgrades in S12; an established commercial regeneration offer in S13 demonstrates a real business model.
key_unknown: Pooled regenerable throughput and buyer acceptance versus external/in-unit alternatives.
next_test_if_uwt: Batch 04 commercial reviewer, 60 minutes: review recent spent-catalyst/regeneration awards at the three refineries; obtain annual eligible lot volumes and comparative off-site commercial quotes.
pass_condition_if_uwt: Pooled repeat contracts load a viable plant and delivered fee/performance beats existing services or replacement.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: PARK if most volumes are internally regenerated, unsuitable, or too fragmented for utilisation; FAIL only on an evidenced mandatory permit/access impossibility.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT; a narrow purchasing/throughput test can validate or falsify the local-service mechanism.

investor_capital_decision: Seed company funds sugar-beet seed multiplication/processing; no breeder licence or site committed.
buyer_market: Kazakh beet growers and their sugar mills; regional seed-export route not established.
why_now: FACT: local beet acreage exists and a 2026 regional increase is reported; old seed self-sufficiency numbers are not current purchasing evidence.
strongest_realistic_alternative: KWS and other established breeders supplying Kazakhstan from their existing production networks.
deciding_location_factor: Breeder rights, reliable saleable output and cost at the required seed scale.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: seed freight savings alone offer limited location rent versus established imported breeder products; local land is not sufficient.
scale_view: Zhambyl reports 9.9 kha in 2026, a regional—not national—figure; no larger reachable contracted seed market demonstrated.
physical_constraint_view: Land/water and commercial seed-certification access unverified; no agronomic experimentation conducted.
captured_status: KWS has an active Kazakhstan portfolio. Presence is not proof of full market capture.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: licensed seed sales/multiplication fee; depends on breeder allocation rather than sugar import share.
cheapest_kill_test: Would a breeder allocate meaningful contracted multiplication here instead of supplying existing networks?
decisive_evidence: FACT: active KWS 2025/26 Kazakhstan catalogue (S14); regional acreage (S15). Sugar tonnage is not seed TAM.
key_unknown: Breeder allocation, contract value and regional outlet.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: PARK unchanged hypothesis: limited apparent location differentiation and domestic seed scale do not justify funding this capital-location case now. Reopen on a breeder-backed regional contract, not merely poor seed self-sufficiency.

investor_capital_decision: Veterinary diagnostic-kit manufacturer considers Kazakhstan production; no specific commercial product/site or investor opening established.
buyer_market: State veterinary purchasing and livestock/export supply chains; market access to neighbours unverified.
why_now: FACT: FMD-free-with-vaccination status supports continuing surveillance demand at business level.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Existing domestic product suppliers and licensed imported kits; strongest supplier by purchased kit unresolved.
deciding_location_factor: Unserved accepted purchasing volume and commercially available rights/production slot.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: local replenishment may help; existing domestic product plans prevent assuming an empty market.
scale_view: Required surveillance is not automatically sufficient manufacturing revenue; purchased units and prices UNKNOWN.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: approved commercial site capacity and product-sale eligibility; restricted validation not undertaken.
captured_status: Historical domestic test-product plans exist; neither achieved 2026 output nor a new investor slot is verified.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: repeated kit-sales margin; commercial cost and contractability remain unresolved.
cheapest_kill_test: Do paid procurement lots remain unserved by current domestic/imported products?
decisive_evidence: FACT: WOAH business-level status S03; historical domestic commercial product plans S04. No restricted detail used.
key_unknown: Manual commercial review of procurement, existing supply and an open investable product slot; further validation incomplete.
next_test_if_uwt: Human commercial reviewer, 45 minutes: inspect procurement award values/volumes and supplier business disclosures; determine whether permitted commercial evidence can establish an incremental plant case.
pass_condition_if_uwt: Permitted evidence demonstrates a material accepted product market, an open investment slot and competitive unit margin.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: PARK if existing supply meets demand or contract value cannot sustain investment; FAIL only on independently evidenced fatal commercial facts, never access limits.
screening_rationale: UWT — manual review required due to research-access limitation. No biological validation or methods are part of this pass.

opportunity_name: Industrial bearing production for mining equipment
investor_capital_decision: Bearing maker builds mining-equipment bearing production; product family and site undefined.
buyer_market: Mine and equipment owners purchasing qualified bearings; volumes not established.
why_now: Russia-service disruption in original card remains an unverified assumption; no bearing-specific investment trigger found.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Stepnogorsk bearing plant plus established imported OEM bearings through local distributors; strongest exact SKU supplier unresolved.
deciding_location_factor: Qualified lifetime cost and repeat volume per bearing family.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: existing domestic manufacture already captures generic proximity; a new plant also faces qualification and product-mix costs.
scale_view: Broad mining spend is not a homogeneous bearing market; no concentrated large-volume product family established.
physical_constraint_view: Specialised production know-how, precision equipment and commercial qualification required; no site secured.
captured_status: FACT: domestic manufacturer advertises mining/industrial product ranges. This does not prove every specification is served.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: manufacturing margin on qualified repeat orders; generic local supply provides little additional rent.
cheapest_kill_test: Is there a commercially material bearing family current domestic/import supply cannot serve competitively?
decisive_evidence: FACT (indexed company catalogue): Stepnogorsk serves mining/industrial sectors and offers multiple bearing families, S16; direct page access timed out.
key_unknown: Specific profitable product-family gap, not existence of bearing buyers.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: PARK because undifferentiated entry competes with an existing local manufacturer and imported OEM supply without a convincing new location mechanism. No claim of technical impossibility or full capture.

investor_capital_decision: Conveyor-belt maker funds manufacturing for mining buyers; site and belt family still to be specified by original buyers.
buyer_market: Mining/conveyor operators with repeat replacement demand.
why_now: FACT: 2026 reported Kazakhmys purchases support replacement demand; an unmet shortage is not established.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Imported qualified belts with local stocking and ConBelt service, plus any matching domestic production.
deciding_location_factor: Accepted belt cost per service life, delivery time and annual compatible production volume.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: heavy replacement belts can reward local lead time; stockholding/service already delivers much of that benefit.
scale_view: S18 reports 15,800 metres of planned additional purchases by one buyer; not national demand or necessarily one specification.
physical_constraint_view: Input materials, utilities and commercial mine qualification at a chosen plant not established.
captured_status: Established import/service channels exist; manufacturing capacity/utilisation by belt grade unresolved.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: production margin plus freight/stock savings if compatible repeat volumes load the line.
cheapest_kill_test: Do repeat compatible belt orders exceed line break-even scale after existing supply?
decisive_evidence: FACT: local qualified import/service channel S17; concrete repeat purchasing example S18. Neither establishes shortage.
key_unknown: Aggregated compatible tonnes/value and an actual lead-time or lifetime-cost gap.
next_test_if_uwt: Batch 04 commercial reviewer, 60 minutes: aggregate recent belt purchases by compatible commercial grade at two miners; compare vendor minimum line volume and delivered quotes with stocked incumbent supply.
pass_condition_if_uwt: Contractable repeat volume sustains the line and accepted lifetime cost or delivery savings justify buyers switching from stocked supply.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: PARK if specifications fragment demand below economic scale or existing stock/service removes the premium; FAIL on a proven essential qualification impossibility.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT; repeat bulky consumables create a plausible location mechanism, but the strongest rival is stocked supply, not an overseas factory gate.

investor_capital_decision: Equipment-repair investor funds a Kazakhstan workshop for mine equipment; exact equipment classes/site remain unspecified.
buyer_market: Mine fleet owners paying for repairs and component replacement.
why_now: Original Russia-friction claim unverified; local installed-base maintenance is real but not a new shortage signal.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Eurasian Machinery's Karaganda component repair centre and other local OEM/in-house workshops, before Russia/China shops.
deciding_location_factor: Downtime-adjusted repair price, turnaround and access to accepted components/rights.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: local turnaround can save downtime, but current local competitors share it; a fleet-specific gap is essential.
scale_view: Recurring repair economics plausible; accessible repair orders after incumbent coverage not quantified.
physical_constraint_view: Workshop tooling, staff and OEM component/acceptance access unresolved; no new site assumed.
captured_status: FACT: a component repair centre already exists in Karaganda. No evidence of complete coverage or spare capacity.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: service/parts margin and faster return to operation under repeat fleet contracts.
cheapest_kill_test: Which paid fleet repairs are still sent away or delayed despite existing domestic centres?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S19 lists an operating service network and Karaganda component repair centre, correcting the card's foreign-only comparison.
key_unknown: A repeat outsourced repair basket with a demonstrable turnaround/cost gap versus local incumbents.
next_test_if_uwt: Batch 04 commercial reviewer, 60 minutes: examine two miners' recent repair awards and dispatch destinations; compare turnaround/price for the same component basket with the incumbent local centre.
pass_condition_if_uwt: Repeat contestable work fills minimum workshop capacity and verified downtime savings exceed any price premium.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: PARK if local centres already meet accepted service terms or orders are too fragmented; FAIL if essential OEM access is demonstrably unavailable.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT; specific fleet order/turnaround evidence can still establish an open service investment despite strong incumbency.

investor_capital_decision: Drilling-fluid supplier builds barite-based preparation capacity; no defined plant or barite-rights opening.
buyer_market: Oil drilling buyers are commercially credible; uranium-sector barite purchasing not established.
why_now: Recurring drilling is a demand premise, not a demonstrated new supply gap.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Existing Karazhal barite production plus established drilling-fluid providers; China/India imports for residual demand.
deciding_location_factor: Accepted delivered fluid cost, qualified inputs and contracted service volumes.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: domestic barite already exists, so raw-material proximity does not uniquely justify a new foreign plant.
scale_view: Company advertises 200 kt/year barite design capacity; current output/spare capacity and fluid demand are distinct UNKNOWNs.
physical_constraint_view: Buyer acceptance, material grade and site utilities remain unverified; no new resource ownership assumed.
captured_status: FACT: operating domestic barite plant evidenced by regulator/company; does not prove fluid formulation or every buyer captured.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: formulation/service margin and avoided bulky freight; same mechanism available to incumbents.
cheapest_kill_test: Is there an uncovered fluid contract beyond current domestic barite/service supply?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S20 describes a domestic barite plant; S21 regulator reports activity at it. Capacity is not utilisation.
key_unknown: Distinct product/service gap and oil-buyer contracts; uranium demand must not be assumed.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: PARK the undifferentiated proposal because its local-input mechanism is already available to established suppliers. Reopen on a buyer-backed gap; not FAIL from missing volumes.

investor_capital_decision: Industrial-gas producer funds production/distribution of oxygen, nitrogen and argon; no anchor/site identified.
buyer_market: Metallurgy, chemicals and medical buyers; unallocated anchor demand unproven.
why_now: FACT: Linde/Qarmet signed a new air-separation agreement in Sep 2026; that specific anchor is being addressed.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Incumbent on-site or merchant gas supply and brownfield ASU expansion; Linde is a concrete alternative.
deciding_location_factor: Long-term creditworthy offtake, power cost and short economical delivery radius.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: local delivery is inherent to existing suppliers; no distinct site-linked surplus demand in this hypothesis.
scale_view: Potentially large anchor market, but no incremental uncontracted volumes; national industrial growth is not an anchor contract.
physical_constraint_view: Firm site power, connection and storage/distribution assets unestablished.
captured_status: A signed Qarmet agreement is stronger than an MoU, but is not FID/operation or evidence all gas markets are captured.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: long-term on-site supply margin or merchant distribution margin at high utilisation.
cheapest_kill_test: Is there a creditworthy anchor outside incumbent contracts that can support a new plant?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S22 records the signed anchor project; S23 documents the on-site contract business model, not Kazakhstan-specific contract duration.
key_unknown: Open anchor, volume, price and site power.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: PARK because the generic local-supply thesis lacks differentiation against anchor-linked incumbent expansion. No claim that all possible gas investment is closed.

investor_capital_decision: Feed-premix investor funds local vitamin-containing premix manufacture; no vitamin-synthesis plant is inferred.
buyer_market: Feed mills and livestock/poultry operators; incremental contract basket UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT: UBM plans a 48 kt/year premix programme; existing Kormovik offers domestic premixes.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Kormovik local supply, planned UBM capacity and imported premix; strongest delivered formulation offer unresolved.
deciding_location_factor: Nutritional product acceptance, bought-in ingredient cost and repeat customer scale.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: local formulation/service can work, but it is already provided domestically; grain abundance does not establish cheap vitamins.
scale_view: UBM planned premix capacity is separate from its much larger feed tonnage; neither is addressable unmet demand.
physical_constraint_view: Vitamin/ingredient supply and commercially approved site unresolved; no biological methods reviewed.
captured_status: Operating domestic offer and competing announced investment. UBM plan is not proof of operation or full capture.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: formulation and service margin; no raw-vitamin import saving assumed.
cheapest_kill_test: Can a new entrant win additional repeat premix contracts versus local and planned supply?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S24 official project plan; S25 existing domestic offering. S24's literal no-domestic-producer wording is contradicted by S25.
key_unknown: Residual paid demand and a defensible ingredient/service advantage.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: PARK unchanged generic proposal: incumbent local formulation and competing investment erode its claimed import-substitution rent. Announcements alone do not justify FAIL.

investor_capital_decision: Specialty fertiliser investor funds water-soluble production/formulation; chemistry, route and site unspecified.
buyer_market: Kazakh and Uzbek greenhouse operators; reachable cross-border contract volume unproven.
why_now: Greenhouse-growth trigger in original card remains unverified at product purchasing level.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Yara products through existing Kazakhstan distributors and other established soluble-fertiliser suppliers; Uzbekistan local supply also needs comparison.
deciding_location_factor: Delivered accepted nutrient cost, input purity and repeat customer volume.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: local availability alone is weak against existing distribution; a domestic commodity fertiliser base does not establish suitable soluble inputs.
scale_view: No product-specific addressable market; national fertiliser/greenhouse totals cannot proxy specialised demand.
physical_constraint_view: Suitable inputs, water/utilities and commercially approved product/site unverified.
captured_status: FACT: established Yara range and Kazchem distribution exist; no proof all incremental demand is filled.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: production/formulation margin; little identified location rent if key inputs must still be purchased competitively.
cheapest_kill_test: Does local production offer a feedstock or delivered-cost benefit beyond stocked imports?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S26-S27 establish accessible competing product/distribution offerings, not a new supplier shortage.
key_unknown: Specific input advantage and meaningful customer contracts versus existing distribution.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: PARK because the as-framed local-availability mechanism is weak against established supply and no distinctive input/site rent is identified. Reopen only on a commercial anchor or input advantage.

investor_capital_decision: Container-service investor funds a repair depot; location and owner approval are unresolved.
buyer_market: Container owners/operators paying accepted repairs, not transit cargo shippers by default.
why_now: Transit growth is an unverified repair-demand proxy; no specific 2026 backlog established.
strongest_realistic_alternative: KTZ Express domestic workshops and repositioning containers to existing approved depots; China only where actual flows support it.
deciding_location_factor: Owner-approved repair cost plus avoided repositioning and out-of-service time.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: repairs near a damaged-container concentration can save empty moves; Kazakhstan already has domestic repair workshops.
scale_view: Transit TEU is not paid repair volume; approved jobs per site and minimum workshop scale UNKNOWN.
physical_constraint_view: Terminal access, container-owner recognition, equipment/staff and lease rights must be verified at a real site.
captured_status: Historical KTZ footprint is established; present capacity and remaining regional gaps UNKNOWN.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: paid repair fees and avoided empty repositioning, under owner/depot agreements.
cheapest_kill_test: Is there an approved paid repair backlog at a specific node after existing depot capacity?
decisive_evidence: FACT: KTZ industry publication S28 identifies existing domestic workshops; its 2020 uniqueness claim is not treated as current.
key_unknown: Owner-approved backlog and incremental repositioning saving versus nearest existing depot.
next_test_if_uwt: Batch 04 commercial reviewer, 60 minutes: obtain 12 months of paid/rejected repair jobs and empty repositioning costs from one terminal/owner; map nearest approved depots and spare slots.
pass_condition_if_uwt: Owner-approved repeat jobs cover depot break-even throughput and avoided empty moves/time exceed incremental repair cost.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: PARK if existing depots serve jobs with negligible diversion cost or owners will not allocate volume; FAIL only if necessary site/owner access is demonstrably impossible.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT; a discrete node-level job and empty-move test can establish a viable additional depot without assuming transit equals demand.

investor_capital_decision: Rail-service investor funds wagon repair facilities; wagon classes and location unresolved.
buyer_market: Wagon owners/operators paying scheduled and unscheduled repairs.
why_now: Transit growth may create work but is not evidence of repair backlog or a new capex gap.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Astana Railway Services' existing Kazakhstan depot network and other domestic/in-house repair, rather than China by default.
deciding_location_factor: Accepted repair price, out-of-service time, network location and depot utilisation.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: local repair reduces diversion, but incumbent local depots share the benefit; only a node/class gap creates an opening.
scale_view: Rail throughput cannot be converted to repair revenue without fleet cycles and owner contracts.
physical_constraint_view: Rail siding, land, wagon-class acceptance, spares and staffing at an actual site UNKNOWN.
captured_status: FACT: established four-depot commercial network advertised; spare capacity and coverage not known.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: contracted repair margin and saved diversion/idle time.
cheapest_kill_test: Do existing depots already cover the same wagon classes and locations below entrant break-even cost?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S29 names four operating-depot branches and existing owner customers; no volume or spare-capacity proof.
key_unknown: A contractable wagon-class/node backlog and economically justified new facility.
next_test_if_uwt: Batch 04 commercial reviewer, 60 minutes: review two owners' repair awards and one node's queue/diversion costs; check incumbent spare slots, class approvals and vendor break-even volume.
pass_condition_if_uwt: Accepted repeat jobs support minimum depot utilisation and lower total repair/diversion cost than existing local capacity.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: PARK if incumbents have adequate nearby slots or no owner will commit jobs; FAIL only on verified essential approval/site impossibility.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT; local service economics are plausible, but the comparison must be against the domestic network.

investor_capital_decision: Construction-chemicals investor funds concrete-superplasticiser production; no differentiated product or site established.
buyer_market: Concrete/precast producers and regional construction purchasers.
why_now: Construction growth exists as a general driver; operating incumbent investment already targets it.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Sika's four Kazakhstan factories and other local admixture suppliers, before imported products.
deciding_location_factor: Delivered performance-adjusted price and customer service; production scope versus bought-in concentrate matters.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: local delivery and technical service already belong to an established foreign investor footprint.
scale_view: Concrete/construction value is not admixture TAM; enough residual share for another plant not demonstrated.
physical_constraint_view: Feed supply, product acceptance and site utilities unverified; no manufacturing route assumed.
captured_status: FACT: Sika reports its fourth Kazakhstan plant operating. This is incumbency, not proof of full market capture.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: admixture sales margin and locally tailored service; no unique location advantage established.
cheapest_kill_test: What specific profitable product/territory is not already served by local capacity?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S30 reports a fourth operating factory and local-market demand rationale, rather than an import-only market.
key_unknown: Defensible differentiation and residual buyer contracts.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: PARK because an undifferentiated entrant cannot claim generic local-freight/service savings as new; no evidenced fatal flaw in all admixture investment.

investor_capital_decision: Plasma-products company funds a Kazakhstan fractionation plant; supply rights and site not committed.
buyer_market: Single distributor/public medicine purchasers buying plasma-derived products; non-sensitive commercial analysis only.
why_now: Reported 2026 procurement reform creates a long-term contracting route, primarily using overseas fractionation.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Contract fractionation abroad using existing qualified plants, plus finished-product procurement.
deciding_location_factor: Legally accessible feed volume and contracted product economics versus overseas tolling.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: local value capture could help only if allocable plasma supply and plant scale outweigh existing overseas economies.
scale_view: Domestic medicine imports are not sufficient plant utilisation; allocable annual supply and product offtake UNKNOWN.
physical_constraint_view: Commercial supply rights, cold-chain cost, site and regulatory eligibility unestablished; no laboratory or biological process research performed.
captured_status: Contracting reform reported; no verified local investor opening or complete overseas award established.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: product/toll margin and retained value, conditional on supply and offtake contracts.
cheapest_kill_test: Can a domestic plant obtain enough legally allocable supply instead of using overseas contract capacity?
decisive_evidence: FACT (reported): S31 describes revised order 84 and contracts up to ten years. Primary act S32 could not be fully accessed; domestic eligibility unresolved.
key_unknown: Commercial supply allocation and eligibility under the current procurement route, plus minimum viable scale.
next_test_if_uwt: Human commercial/legal reviewer, 60 minutes: obtain the effective procurement text and business-level allocable annual supply totals; compare a domestic vendor scale/cost indication with overseas tolling terms.
pass_condition_if_uwt: Permitted domestic entry can secure sufficient contracted supply and product offtake to beat the overseas alternative at viable scale.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: PARK if overseas contracts leave insufficient unallocated supply or domestic costs cannot compete; FAIL only on a confirmed binding commercial/legal exclusion.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT at business level; overseas tolling is a concrete rival, not proof a domestic plant is prohibited. No biological validation attempted.

investor_capital_decision: Contract-sterilisation investor funds an electron-beam facility for medical/food customers; site unspecified.
buyer_market: Manufacturers/exporters paying for accepted processing services; eligible saleable throughput UNKNOWN.
why_now: Service need exists; no new uncovered demand trigger established.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Existing Kazakhstan INP commercial facility and other accepted domestic or outsourced services.
deciding_location_factor: Accepted delivered processing cost and facility utilisation at buyer-required service levels.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: avoided international shipment is already available through local facilities; no distinct location gap in the stated proposal.
scale_view: Demand for sterile goods or food exports is not outsourced paid throughput; minimum plant utilisation unestablished.
physical_constraint_view: Commercial product acceptance, licensed site/power and throughput availability UNKNOWN; no operating methods or parameters used.
captured_status: FACT: institutional source offers the same broad commercial service categories domestically; spare capacity unresolved.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: contract-service fee and avoided transport; incumbent has the same proximity mechanism.
cheapest_kill_test: Is there accepted commercial throughput current domestic services cannot handle economically?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S33 establishes existing commercial sterilisation/food-treatment service, not a vacant local market.
key_unknown: Specific customer/location backlog beyond existing providers.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: PARK unchanged proposal because local-service savings are not distinctive against existing domestic provision. No assertion all future capacity is captured.

investor_capital_decision: Water-chemical investor funds coagulant manufacture; chemistry, site and usable aluminium feed unresolved.
buyer_market: Municipal water utilities with recurrent tendered purchases.
why_now: No special why-now established; recurring purchases create a testable industrial customer base.
strongest_realistic_alternative: ASCOR's Pavlodar supply and other accepted domestic/imported coagulants; strongest quote is utility/site-specific.
deciding_location_factor: Accepted delivered treatment cost, including concentration, freight and supplier terms.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: heavy reagent freight may create a regional cost wedge, but aluminium availability alone is not a feedstock advantage.
scale_view: Procurement confirms a paying buyer class; residual annual tonnes at a viable plant UNKNOWN.
physical_constraint_view: Appropriate feed, acid/chemical access, water/power and commercial approvals at a specific site not secured.
captured_status: FACT: ASCOR participates in municipal procurement and domestic production is reported; not proof every region is served competitively.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: recurring reagent margin plus avoided delivered freight if a regional production gap exists.
cheapest_kill_test: Is a utility's delivered-price gap large enough for a viable plant versus existing domestic supply?
decisive_evidence: FACT: procurement record S34 shows real coagulant competition; S35 reports existing Pavlodar domestic supply. No contract award inferred from a complaint.
key_unknown: Usable feed cost and contracted regional tonnes versus lowest accepted incumbent delivered cost.
next_test_if_uwt: Batch 04 commercial reviewer, 60 minutes: compare two utilities' recent accepted purchase quantities/prices with domestic delivered quotes and local input/plant cost indications on the same commercial basis.
pass_condition_if_uwt: Repeat contractable volume loads minimum capacity and accepted delivered treatment cost beats incumbent supply after all inputs and freight.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: PARK if incumbents match delivered cost or volumes cannot load capacity; FAIL only if a necessary feed/approval is demonstrably unavailable.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT; a buyer-specific delivered-cost test is cheap and a bulk-chemical freight mechanism remains plausible.

opportunity_name: Coal-fleet steam-turbine and boiler repair centre
investor_capital_decision: Non-Russian OEM/service investor funds coal-fleet steam-turbine/boiler repair and parts workshop in Pavlodar-Karaganda cluster.
buyer_market: Power-plant owners buying overhaul/parts under repeat service contracts; all-repair budget is not turbine-only TAM.
why_now: FACT: 2026 national plan covers 51 turbines and 55 boilers; supplier disruption is not freshly established across all owners.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Karaganda Turbomechanical Plant, Energo Spets Stroy at Ekibastuz and internal repair, before foreign OEM shops.
deciding_location_factor: Accepted parts/repair turnaround in the outage window and contractable utilisation versus existing local shops.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: local proximity is real but already provided by named domestic workshops; foreign technology must solve a residual gap.
scale_view: Installed base gives recurrent demand; national counts include multiple equipment types and are not an available contract backlog.
physical_constraint_view: Site skills/tooling, parts rights and owner acceptance unestablished for entrant; existing workshops prove capability exists, not spare slots.
captured_status: FACT: operating domestic repair capacity with named plant references; absence of a foreign-branded shop does not imply an empty market.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: repeat repair/parts margin and reduced downtime only where incumbent service cannot meet the same requirement.
cheapest_kill_test: Which specific accepted repair/parts jobs cannot domestic shops perform on time at competitive cost?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S36 repair plan; S37 named domestic repair clients; S38 existing Ekibastuz workshop. These undermine a foreign-only rival comparison.
key_unknown: Profitable residual work and a technology/turnaround advantage beyond domestic incumbent capacity.
next_test_if_uwt: Batch 04 commercial reviewer, 75 minutes: inspect five recent steam-turbine/boiler repair awards and delayed/outsourced parts lots; compare incumbent capabilities/queues and one owner's acceptance requirements.
pass_condition_if_uwt: A repeated accepted parts/repair basket remains unserved or late despite local workshops, and anchor contracts support entrant break-even utilisation at a defensible premium/cost.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: PARK if local suppliers meet the same requirements or residual basket is too small; FAIL if essential rights/owner acceptance cannot be obtained.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT; large repair need survives, but the central proximity advantage is not unique. No inference from total repair budgets to available revenue.

investor_capital_decision: Strategic base-metal investor acquires a Shalkiya stake and funds completion at Zhanakorgan, Kyzylorda.
buyer_market: Domestic/Chinese smelters buying concentrate; signed offtake and payable terms not established.
why_now: FACT: Zijin expressed participation interest in Sep 2026; state asset passport still considers a strategic partner.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Acquire/expand an operating zinc asset or buy concentrate rather than finish a delayed mine; strongest competing named asset not established.
deciding_location_factor: Acquisition price plus remaining capex and cost per payable metal unit versus operating-asset alternatives.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: existing mine works can lower entry cost, but sunk spending provides no advantage if recovery/completion costs are poor.
scale_view: Historical project planned 4 Mt/year ore; ore throughput is not metal revenue. Grade/recovery and completion budget need current verification.
physical_constraint_view: Power/water, permits and remaining infrastructure cannot be inferred from historical financing or mine works.
captured_status: July ownership disclosure retains state sole shareholder; September interest is not a sale/FID. Equity opening remains plausible, exact terms unknown.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: completion discount and concentrate margin if purchase price, recovery and remaining capex permit it.
cheapest_kill_test: Does current total entry cost work after low-grade/recovery and funding reset?
decisive_evidence: FACT: current interest S39, ownership S40, partner consideration S41. FACT (reported): EBRD loan repaid in Dec 2024, S42, consistent with indexed S43 and historical loan status S44.
key_unknown: Current stake/valuation, recoverable payable metal, remaining capex and shareholder debt; strongest asset alternative unresolved.
next_test_if_uwt: Batch 04 commercial reviewer, 90 minutes: reconcile latest issuer debt/capex notes with sale terms; obtain remaining-cost and recovery/payability ranges; compare total cost per payable tonne with one operating zinc-asset/brownfield alternative.
pass_condition_if_uwt: An open stake at credible terms plus independently supported recovery and remaining-cost ranges shows a competitive completion margin after debt and logistics.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: PARK if valuation/completion cost loses to operating assets or financing timetable is unworkable; FAIL on a closed sale or evidenced irreparable recovery/physical flaw.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT; a real entry decision survives, but stale EBRD financing and headline ore capacity cannot support a cheap PASS on completion economics.

investor_capital_decision: Synthetic-rubber/petrochemical investor takes equity and helps finance the existing Atyrau Butadiene complex; offered stake unconfirmed.
buyer_market: Tyre and petrochemical buyers; Tengri Tyres is a source-card buyer candidate, not verified binding offtake.
why_now: FACT: project is now state-sponsored with a March 2026 Sinopec EPC; July bond funding is reported. Former sponsor exit does not prove a sale invitation.
strongest_realistic_alternative: State retains/finances the plant, or buyer imports established rubber supply; strongest alternative producer/site not established.
deciding_location_factor: Available equity terms, enforceable feed price and product spreads/offtake versus imports.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: existing feed/infrastructure may help; the card's cheap-butane formula is an unverified analyst estimate, not a bankable cost.
scale_view: Sponsor states over 300 kt/year across five products, not 300 kt of rubber. Current saleable product split unresolved.
physical_constraint_view: EPC signed; feed delivery, utilities, licence continuation and construction/completion funding need contractual confirmation.
captured_status: State ownership and signed EPC evidenced; no foreign-equity invitation verified. Debt programme is not fully committed project finance.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: feed-to-product margin plus equity entry terms; cannot assume the former 75% stake is being offered.
cheapest_kill_test: Does the current owner actually offer an investable stake or require a new equity partner?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S45 signed EPC/state sponsor/2029 target; S46 reports bond programme and first tranche separately; S47 is only a historical technology award.
key_unknown: Open partner mandate first; then product-specific offtake, feed terms, licence and competitive margin.
next_test_if_uwt: Batch 04 commercial reviewer, 60 minutes: seek public owner partner mandate/current financing terms; reconcile product slate and feed/offtake terms, then compare indicative delivered rubber economics with an incumbent supplier quote.
pass_condition_if_uwt: Owner confirms a real equity opening and transferable feed/licence/offtake terms support a margin competitive with imports within remaining funding needs.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: PARK if owner intends fully funded state retention or competitive spreads are inadequate; FAIL if the specified equity opening is demonstrably closed or an essential licence/feed right unavailable.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT; real capital deployment exists, but an exited shareholder and bridge finance are not evidence of a currently available ownership opening.

opportunity_name: Certified intermediate-crop oil for EU-compliant SAF
investor_capital_decision: Oilseed/renewable-feedstock investor funds contract supply, certification and crushing/pretreatment in northern Kazakhstan for EU SAF buyers.
buyer_market: HEFA/SAF feedstock buyers paying for accepted advanced-category oil; certification premium and committed volume UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT: 2024 EU amendment adds conditional intermediate-crop aviation feedstock; current implementing treatment of this Kazakh rotation not verified.
strongest_realistic_alternative: French/EU intermediate-crop chains, including Avril/TotalEnergies; Argentine Bunge/Chevron platform is a serious contingent rival, not assumed disqualified.
deciding_location_factor: Certifiable accepted oil volume and delivered netback after logistics, audit and crop-rotation costs.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: northern single-harvest geography may matter but is not automatic eligibility; existing oilseed exports cannot confer advanced-feedstock status.
scale_view: Source assumptions: 50-100 kt/year oil and 0.15-0.35 t/ha. CALCULATION: 100 kt needs about 0.29-0.67 Mha; not verified available land.
physical_constraint_view: Suitable contracted land, water/crop economics, export route reliability and buyer acceptance unresolved; no crop experiments conducted.
captured_status: EU and Argentine investments exist; no verified closed Kazakh certified-oil slot. Neither foreign acquisition nor an SAF MoU proves capture here.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: certified-oil netback premium must cover incremental supply, logistics and land-opportunity costs.
cheapest_kill_test: Can the exact Kazakh rotation qualify under effective rules, and does any premium survive delivered costs?
decisive_evidence: FACT: official indexed legal clause S48; contemporary rule uncertainty S49; real rival supply-chain investment S50-S51. No current certification opinion obtained.
key_unknown: Legal eligibility of fallow replacement, current rule text and certification; then buyer premium and delivered volume economics.
next_test_if_uwt: Human commercial/legal reviewer, 90 minutes: verify effective EU implementing text and obtain a certification-scheme eligibility opinion for the stated rotation; then compare one buyer's indicative accepted-oil netback with all-in logistics/audit/opportunity cost. No outreach sent in this task.
pass_condition_if_uwt: Written eligibility under effective rules plus buyer-accepted volumes and conservative delivered netback competitive with EU/Argentine alternatives; no assumed certification premium.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: FAIL if effective rules definitively exclude the exact product model; PARK if premium/timing or land economics cannot cover incremental costs. Rival eligibility alone is not fatal without a cost comparison.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT; conditional regulatory value is testable, but a northern climate or generic ISCC precedent cannot establish qualification. Do not automatically kill on a rival-rule change; test resulting netback.
